question: In the rate test, what capacities did NFA-A and NFA-F recover at 0.1C after the 1C step, against their initial 0.1C capacities, and what losses does the paper give for each?
rendered:
The paper states that the NFA-A variant delivered a capacity of ≈116 mAh g^− 1 at high C-rates of 1C when compared with the NFA-F variant (≈81 mAh g^− 1) at the same rate. 

After lowering the C-rate from 1C to 0.1C, the NFA-A variant achieved a capacity of ≈170 mAh g^− 1, which was similar (≈5%) to the initial capacity observed at 0.1C (≈184 mAh g^− 1) prior to rate capability tests. 

Comparatively, the NFA-F variant delivered a low capacity of ≈138 mAh g^− 1 when compared with the initial capacity of ≈190 mAh g^− 1, resulting in ≈27% loss.

So, NFA-A recovered ≈5% of its initial capacity at 0.1C, while NFA-F suffered ≈27% loss.
